description: Machine-readable registry of QVF canonical section kinds and registered vendor namespaces. Governed per GOVERNANCE.md; the canonical_kinds list is drift-guarded against spec/qvf_manifest.schema.json.

steward.name: vibe-qc
steward.note: QVF was created by and is stewarded by the vibe-qc project. The spec and reference implementations are Apache-2.0 and the format is producer-neutral; see GOVERNANCE.md.

version_decisions.summary: Withdrawn: the whole schema-visible delta was one optional member (`lattice` on `reaction.path`), which is the additive case and must not bump qvf_version. `lattice` is now an optional member of v1; a periodic reaction path is detected by its presence.
version_decisions.compatibility: Producers MUST NOT emit qvf_version 2. Consumers SHOULD accept it and treat it as 1 (archives already exist in the wild). qvf_manifest_v2.schema.json is retained as a frozen artifact resolving its $id; it is a strict superset of v1.

vendor_namespaces.purpose: First-party vendor data that is not part of the visualization contract: restart-only per-k complex Bloch wavefunctions (x_vibeqc.bloch_wavefunction) and live-checkpoint hints.
ORCA-specific data with no canonical kind. (EPR started here as x_orca.epr and was promoted to the canonical spectra.epr kind.)

promotions.note: Added directly by maintainer decision (GOVERNANCE.md, Change process: clear ecosystem need + reference consumer). Declarative specification of the calculation an archive requests (job_type, method, basis, functional, charge, multiplicity, kpoints, tasks, options), making a QVF archive an executable input a runner can execute and update in place. Complements run.record — the request vs. the record of what ran. Carries data, never code.

Added directly by maintainer decision (GOVERNANCE.md, Change process: clear ecosystem need + reference consumer). Carries the verbatim program input, full log/output, and auxiliary attachments of one program invocation, making a QVF archive a self-contained record of a calculation. Producer-neutral: the section's `program` field names the code that ran, independent of root `source.program`.
Promoted by maintainer decision ahead of the two-producer threshold to give ORCA a canonical target for EPR (g-tensor / hyperfine / zero-field-splitting).
